title: PM to release the Autobiography of Former President Shri Ram Nath Kovind on 12 August
subtitle: Title of the Autobiography: “Triumph of the Indian Republic: My Life, My Struggles”
body_text:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi will release the autobiography of former President of India, Shri Ram Nath Kovind, titled “Triumph of the Indian Republic: My Life, My Struggles”, on 12 August, 2026, at 9:30 AM at Vigyan Bhavan, New Delhi. Prime Minister will also address the gathering on the occasion.
The release of the autobiography by the Prime Minister will mark a significant occasion celebrating the life and contributions of one of India’s most distinguished public figures. The autobiography offers a deeply personal account of Shri Ram Nath Kovind’s remarkable life journey, tracing his experiences, struggles and achievements from his early years to his distinguished public life and eventual service as the 14th President of India. The book provides insights into the values, experiences and circumstances that shaped his journey and public service.

enrichment.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will release former President Ram Nath Kovind's autobiography, titled 'Triumph of the Indian Republic: My Life, My Struggles', on 12 August 2026 at Vigyan Bhavan, New Delhi. The Prime Minister will also address the gathering at the event. The book chronicles Kovind's life journey from his early years to his tenure as the 14th President of India.
enrichment.context:
Ram Nath Kovind served as the 14th President of India from 2017 to 2022, prior to which he was Governor of Bihar and a Rajya Sabha member. He is notable for being only the second Dalit to hold the office of President, after K.R. Narayanan, and his tenure saw significant events including the abrogation of Article 370 and the passage of major legislations. He later chaired the high-level committee examining the feasibility of 'One Nation, One Election', a significant ongoing constitutional and electoral reform debate in India.

Such book releases by sitting Prime Ministers for former Presidents are largely ceremonial in nature, reflecting institutional courtesy and continuity in India's constitutional framework, but they also serve to highlight public figures' contributions to nation-building and can offer insights into the functioning of the highest constitutional office, which is relevant background for understanding the Indian polity.

prelims_questions.question: Ram Nath Kovind, whose autobiography was released by PM Modi, served as which numbered President of India?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release explicitly states Ram Nath Kovind served as the 14th President of India.

prelims_questions.question: Before becoming President of India, Ram Nath Kovind served as Governor of which state?
prelims_questions.explanation: Ram Nath Kovind was Governor of Bihar before being elected as the 14th President of India, a well-established fact about his public career.
